name: Nazca culture
summary: A culture of the dry southern coast of Peru known for the giant Nazca Lines drawn in the desert, fine painted pottery and underground aqueducts that still work today.

location.value: The river valleys of the Rio Grande de Nazca and the Ica Valley on Peru’s southern coast.

terrain.value: One of the driest deserts on Earth, crossed by short rivers.

climate.value: Extremely dry; rivers flow only part of the year.

resources.value: River water and underground aqueducts (puquios) fed crops such as maize, beans and cotton; fish from the coast.

disasters.value: Long droughts and El Niño floods; deforestation of huarango trees may have made floods worse.

urbanisation.value: Cahuachi was a ceremonial centre rather than a city.

disease.value: Unknown; skeletons show some signs of malnutrition and injuries.

migration.value: Unknown; the Nazca developed from the earlier Paracas culture in the same region.

economicBase.value: Subsistence was based largely on agriculture: maize, squash, sweet potato, manioc, achira, beans and cotton, with fish in small amounts; puquios (underground aqueducts) supplied water.

tradeRoutes.value: Contact with highland peoples for wool, obsidian and other goods.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible; fine textiles and pottery show skilled craftwork.

moneyAndTax.value: No money is known; labour for projects may have been owed to leaders.

inequality.value: Some richer burials with fine pottery and textiles suggest an elite.

governmentType.value: Local chiefdoms and regional centres of power; no formal governing system is described.

keyRulers.value: No rulers are known; Nazca had no writing.

institutions.value: The ceremonial centre of Cahuachi, with adobe mounds, used for gatherings and rituals rather than as a city.

stability.value: Lasted about 900 years (about 100 BCE–800 CE) before declining.

eliteConflict.value: Unknown; there is no direct evidence of rival elites.

armyAndTech.value: Trophy heads (prepared human heads) suggest raids or ritual warfare; weapons included clubs and spear-throwers.

majorWars.value: Unknown; no specific wars are recorded.

territoryChange.value: Centred on the Nazca and Ica valleys of Peru’s southern coast; little evidence of expansion.

alliancesRivals.value: Unknown; later came under the influence of the Wari Empire.

inventions.value: Puquios, underground aqueducts, several dozen still in use.

scienceEducation.value: No writing; skill in water engineering and in laying out lines across the desert.

openness.value: Strongly influenced by the earlier Paracas culture.

communicationTransport.value: Travel on foot and with llamas between the coast and the highlands.

religion.value: Beliefs were based on agriculture and fertility, with feasting and rituals at Cahuachi and severed trophy heads in rituals. The killer whale being is not named in the part read.

languageWriting.value: No writing; their language is unknown.

artsArchitecture.value: The Nazca Lines (huge figures and lines drawn on the desert) and brightly painted pottery.

socialStructure.value: Unknown in detail; probably farmers, craftspeople and a ritual elite.

sharedIdentity.value: A shared style of pottery and textiles across the valleys.

dailyLife.value: Houses of cane and adobe; maize, beans, squash and fish; fine cotton textiles.

neighbours.value: Grew out of the Paracas culture; later influenced by the Wari Empire.

ideasReligions.value: Unknown; Nazca art styles influenced nearby areas.

colonisation.value: None; it did not found colonies.

riseSignals.value: Grew from the Paracas culture around 100 BCE.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Nazca culture (checked 6 Nov 2026); Silverman & Proulx, The Nasca (2002)

peakPeriod.value: The culture flourished from about 100 BC to AD 800; the page names no peak. The decline is thought to have followed El Niño flooding made worse by the cutting of Prosopis pallida trees.

declineSignals.value: Climate stress (drought and El Niño) and the expansion of the Wari.

outcome.value: Declined around 800 CE, perhaps because of floods, drought and Wari influence; later peoples lived in the area.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Nazca culture (checked 6 Nov 2026); Silverman & Proulx, The Nasca (2002)

overallCertainty.value: Low to medium. The purpose of the lines is unknown.

knownFor.label: Nazca Lines
knownFor.note: Giant figures drawn in the desert.
